summary: Sage separates assistive AI use (language, grammar, structure), which needs no disclosure, from generative AI use that affects content, methods, results or images, which must be disclosed and verified by authors. Reviewers may use GenAI to help write and format reports but must not upload manuscripts to AI tools. Editors must not use GenAI for decision letters, summaries of unpublished research, or editorial work.

evidence.quote: AI tools that make suggestions to improve or enhance your own work, such as tools to improve language, grammar, or structure
must be disclosed upon submission so the editorial team can evaluate the content generated.
Generated images that are presented as unique or novel research images
Peer reviewers may use generative AI (GenAI) to help write and format the peer review reports
such as uploading or copy-pasting the manuscript or parts of it to a GenAI tool
Editors must not use ChatGPT or other GenAI to generate decision letters, or summaries of unpublished research.
